rationale: No story/spec artifact exists for this change (no-spec mode) — confidence forced low per policy. Blind and edge-case lenses ran; acceptance was correctly skipped (no-spec, not a failure). One real, unambiguous defect (CR-001): the new X-CodeMie-Chrome-Extension header is missing from proxy_router.py's PROXY_HOP_BY_HOP_HEADERS set, so unlike every other CodeMie-specific identity header (X-CodeMie-CLI, X-CodeMie-Client, etc.) it is forwarded verbatim to the upstream LLM provider. 6 other raised concerns were triaged to defer/dismiss and are not emitted: (1) chrome_extension_request has no cross-check against cli_request/client_type — deliberately rejected; this exact ticket's review history explicitly removed prior mismatch-detection/cross-validation logic between these two independent headers as unwanted complexity, and the real client (extension) never sends both headers together, so re-adding a cross-check would contradict the established design decision (dismiss); (2) header-recognition logic implemented in 3 files (metrics.py, proxy_router.py, llm_proxy_monitoring_service.py) — mirrors the pre-existing pattern for X-CodeMie-CLI/X-CodeMie-Client, not a new anti-pattern (defer); (3) no length cap on the chrome_extension string — false positive, both write paths already truncate generically (BaseMonitoringService.send_count_metric applies limit_string to every string attribute; llm_proxy_monitoring_service's _sanitize_request_info caps at 500 chars) (dismiss); (4) test for the PLATFORM-billing outcome doesn't assert_called_with on the mocked get_category_budget_id — mirrors the exact pattern of the pre-existing sibling test test_web_request_uses_platform_even_when_cli_budget_configured in the same file (defer); (5) metric-name-prefix logic in metrics.py doesn't consult the new header — the documented contract ties that behavior to X-CodeMie-Client specifically, which the real client always sends alongside the new header, so this is unreachable in practice (dismiss); (6) large narrative doc with cross-repo deployment claims / historical data left uncorrected — explicitly stated non-goals in the doc, not code defects (dismiss).

findings.title: New header missing from hop-by-hop strip set
findings.problem: PROXY_HOP_BY_HOP_HEADERS explicitly lists every CodeMie-specific identity header (HEADER_CODEMIE_CLI, HEADER_CODEMIE_CLIENT, HEADER_CODEMIE_SESSION_ID, etc., lines 130-138) so they are stripped before the request is forwarded to the upstream LLM provider. HEADER_CODEMIE_CHROME_EXTENSION, added by this diff, was not added to that set.
findings.impact: Every Chrome-extension request forwards X-CodeMie-Chrome-Extension verbatim to the upstream LLM provider (Azure/OpenAI/etc.), unlike every sibling CodeMie header. Low-sensitivity (a version string), but it is an internal implementation detail leaking to a third party and breaks the established convention this same file enforces for every other custom header.
findings.recommendation: Add HEADER_CODEMIE_CHROME_EXTENSION.lower() to PROXY_HOP_BY_HOP_HEADERS alongside the other HEADER_CODEMIE_* entries.
